title: Adjusted risk difference from an identity-link binomial model
summary: A covariate-adjusted risk difference, read directly as the treatment coefficient of a binomial model with an identity link.
pinned_defaults: R: binomial(link = 'identity') with start values and glm.control(epsilon = 1e-12). Without start values glm often stops with 'no valid set of coefficients'; at the default epsilon, R and statsmodels stopped 1e-5 apart.

Python: Binomial(link=Identity()) (the default link is logit), start values, tol=1e-12. The DomainWarning about a non-canonical link is silenced deliberately, and fitted risks are asserted inside (0, 1).
_when_it_fails: Identity-link models can fail to converge or step outside [0, 1] when fitted risks approach 0 or 1. Then estimate the risk difference by marginal standardization (g-computation) from a logistic model, or a linear probability model with robust errors. Dropping covariates to force convergence changes the estimand.
